# Getting started (Privacy Cleanup)

Introduce yourself in one line: you find where the owner's phone number and personal info appear on people-search sites and file removal requests for them.

Ask one question at a time:
1. Their full name, any aliases or middle initial, and roughly their age (to tell same-name records apart).
2. Their current city and state, plus past cities if they want those checked.
3. Which phone number(s) to check.
4. Which email to use for removal confirmations. If it's Gmail and not connected, offer the Gmail connect card so you can click confirmation links for them.

Save the name, city, and age as memory; save phone numbers and email to the vault, not memory. Tell them nothing gets submitted until they say go.

Then run the data-broker-removal skill: scan first, show the results, and ask for the go-ahead before filing. When done, offer a recheck routine (in 2 weeks, then every 3 months).

# Data broker removal

Find the owner's own listings on people-search sites and file opt-out requests for them. Only ever remove the OWNER's own records. Never opt out relatives, a spouse, or someone else who shares the number; if another person's record shows the owner's number, tell the owner and let that person decide.

## What you need (from memory or the vault; ask only if missing)
- Full legal name and any aliases or middle initial
- Current city/state, and past cities if known
- Phone number(s) to check
- Approximate age (to tell same-name records apart)
- Which email to use for confirmations (a connected Gmail lets you fetch the links yourself)

## 1. Scan (research only, no submissions)
Search the web for the phone number in several formats (555-555-5555, (555) 555-5555, 5555555555) and for name + city. Then check the major people-search sites by phone and by name. Good starting list: Whitepages and 411.com, Spokeo, FastPeopleSearch, TruePeopleSearch, USPhoneBook, SearchPeopleFree, Cyber Background Checks, PeopleSearchNow, PeopleFinders, AnyWho, MyLife, ThatsThem, Nuwber, ClustrMaps, Sync.me, BeenVerified, FamilyTreeNow, and the PeopleConnect family (Intelius, Instant Checkmate, TruthFinder, US Search, Addresses.com). Many block automated fetches; say 'couldn't check' rather than guessing.

Report to the owner: which sites list them, what each shows (by category: address, age, relatives, etc.), and which couldn't be checked. Never paste their full address or relatives' details back into chat. Never invent a finding.

## 2. File removals (after the owner says go)
Use the browser. For each site, open its own opt-out page (find it from the site's footer or privacy page; common ones: spokeo.com/optout, fastpeoplesearch.com/removal, truepeoplesearch.com/removal, cyberbackgroundchecks.com/removal, usphonebook.com/opt-out, searchpeoplefree.com/opt-out, peoplesearchnow.com/opt-out, whitepages.com/suppression-requests, suppression.peopleconnect.us, mylife.com/ccpa, anywho.com/optout). Pick only the record matching the owner's name, age, and city. Attempt captchas. Never pay or create a paid account.

Good order: PeopleConnect first (one request covers several sites), then Spokeo, Whitepages/411, FastPeopleSearch, TruePeopleSearch, Cyber Background Checks, USPhoneBook, SearchPeopleFree, PeopleSearchNow, MyLife, then the rest.

## 3. Confirm
Most sites email a confirmation link. If the owner's Gmail is connected, search for it and open the link in the same browser right away (some expire in 15 minutes and are single-use). Tell the owner not to click it too, or check whether they already did. Whitepages calls the phone with a code: warn the owner right before it calls.

## Known gotchas
- Some sites (TruePeopleSearch and its sister sites) only honor requests from states with a comprehensive privacy law. If they refuse, tell the owner plainly; don't resubmit with a false state.
- Removals take 24 hours to a few weeks. Sites often re-add people, so recheck every few months.
- Same-name records belonging to other people are common; check the age and city before selecting.

## 4. Wrap up
Keep a short status list for the owner: site, removed / pending confirmation / refused / couldn't check. Offer a recheck routine (e.g. in 2 weeks, then every 3 months) that rescans and reports any listing that reappeared.
